dev-notes:
The ontology has these top-level elements:
1. `metadata`: General metadata about the ontology. See [Metadata](#Metadata) section.
2. `types`: Entity type definitions. See [Types](#Types) section.
3. `composites`: Non-primitive type definitions referenced by entity fields. See [Composites](#Composites) section.
4. `enums`: Enumerations referenced by entity fields. See [Enums](#Enums) section.
5. `taxonomies`: Taxonomies referenced by entity fields. See [Taxonomies](#Taxonomies) section.
6. `dev-notes`: These notes (don't we all loooove self-references)

# Metadata
Metadata has the following general structure:
```
"metadata": {
   "kg-version": "175",
   "binary-version": "0.3.15",
   "generated": "1613687623"
}
```
1. `kg-version`: Version of the KG for which this ontology was generated
2. `binary-version`: Internal developer metadata
3. `generated`: Unix timestamp when this metadata was generated

# Types
Type definitions have the following general structure:
```
"Person": {
   "name": "Person",
   "typeHierarchy": [
      "DiffbotEntity"
   ],
   "taxonomy": null,
   "fields": {
      "twitterUri": {
         "name": "twitterUri",
         "description": "Link to the Twitter profile of the Person entity",
         "isFact": true,
         "isEnum": false,
         "isList": false,
         "isPrimitive": false,
         "type": "DiffbotUrl",
         "isDeprecated": false
      },
      ...
   }
}
```
1. `name`: Name of the entity
2. `typeHierarchy`: Type hierarchy of the entity. `DiffbotEntity` is the root type. An entity inherits all fields from its hierarchy. The `typeHierarchy` is ordered from closest to farthest ancestor. Example:
```
   "LocalBusiness": {
      "typeHierarchy": [
         "Organization",
         "DiffbotEntity"
      ],
```
3. `taxonomy`: Refers to a taxonomy for this entity, if one exists. See [Taxonomies](#Taxonomies) section. 
4. `fields`: Entity fields. See [Fields section](#Fields).

### Fields
Entity fields have the following general structure:
```
   "categories":{
      "name":"categories",
      "description":"Industry categories",
      "isFact":true,
      "isEnum":false,
      "isList":true,
      "isPrimitive":false,
      "type":"LinkedEntity",
      "leType":[
         "IndustryCategory"
      ],
      "isDeprecated":false
   }
```
1. `name`: Name of the field
2. `description`: Description of the field
3. `isFact`: A value of `true` indicates that this field is a Fact field. Fact fields contain provenance and confidence information, aside from the value of the fact. See [Facts](#Facts) section for structure of fact.
4. `isEnum`: A value of `true` indicates that this field is an enumeration. Enumeration values are listed in the `enum` section of the ontology. See section on [Enums](#Enums) .
5. `isList`: A value of `true` indicates that this field is an array field and can hold multiple values.
6. `isPrimitive`: A value of `true` indicates that this field is a primitive. See sections on [Primitives](#Primitives)  and [Composites](#Composites) for more information on field datatypes.
7. `type`: Type of the field. Fields can be [Primitives](#Primitives), [Composites](#Composites), [Enums](#Enums) or one of the [Entity Types](#Types).
8. `leType`: Indicates that this fields refers to a LinkedEntity and lists the Entity Types that this LinkedEntity can refer to. See section on [LinkedEntity](#LinkedEntity) for details.
9. `isDeprecated`: Indicates if the field is deprecated and may not be supported in the future.

### Facts
Fact fields contain provenance and confidence information, aside from the value of the fact. Fact fields have the following general structure:
```
"twitterUri": {
   "explicitOrigin": [
      "angel.co/diffbot",
      "crunchbase.com/organization/diffbot",
      "wikidata.org/entity/Q17052069"
   ],
   "confidence": "0.60",
   "value": "twitter.com/diffbot"
}
```
### Primitives
The following primitives types are supported:
- `Integer`: Integer types such as `byte`, `short`, `int`, `long`
- `Float`: Decimal types such as `float`, `double`
- `Boolean`: Boolean type
- `String`: String type
- `URL`: This is a special type of String which represents a URL

### LinkedEntity
LinkedEntity fields refer to other other Entity Types. For example, a `Organization.founders` is a LinkedEntity that refers to `Person` type.

LinkedEntities have the `type` fields declared as `LinkedEntity` and the possible Entity Types are listed in the `leType` element.
```
   "type": "LinkedEntity",
   "leType": [ "Person" ],
```

# Composites
Composites are complex datatypes. They have the following general structure:
```
   "Contact":{
      "name":"Contact",
      "fields":{
         "contactString":{
            "name":"contactString",
            "description":"A field such as email address etc.",
            "isFact":false,
            "isEnum":false,
            "isList":false,
            "isPrimitive":true,
            "type":"String",
            "isDeprecated":false
         },
         ...
      }
   }
```
1. `name`: Name of the Composite
2. `description`: Description of the Composite
3. `fields`: Composite fields. They have the same structure as an Entity field. See [Fields section](#Fields).
 
# Enums
Enums have the following general structure:
```
   "EyeColor":{
      "name":"EyeColor",
      "values":[
         "Black",
         "Brown",
         "Blue",
         ...
      ]
   }
```
1. `name`: Name of the Enum
2. `description`: Description of the Enum
3. `values`: Possible values of the composite

# Taxonomies
If an Entity Type has an associated taxonomy, it'll be mentioned in the `taxonomy` field of the Type definition. The taxonomy definition itself is under the top-level `taxonomies` element.

```
   "IndustryCategory":{
      "name":"IndustryCategory",
      "taxonomy": "IndustryCategory",
      "typeHierarchy":[
         "Intangible",
         "DiffbotEntity"
      ]
   }
```

Taxonomies have the following general structure:
```
[
   {
      "name":"Food And Drink Companies",
      "diffbotId": "EXXXXXXXXXXX",
      "info": {
         "naicsMapping":"311000"
      }
      "children":[
         {
            "name": "Animal Food Manufacturers",
            "info": {
               "naicsMapping":"311000"
            }
            "children":[
                ...
            ]
         }
      ]
   },
   ...
]
```
1. `name`: Name of the category
2. `diffbotId`: DiffbotId of the category, if an entity exists in Diffbot KG corresponding to the category
3. `info`: Information specific to the taxonomy. The structure of this element is not formally defined and can change depending on the specific taxonomy.
4. `children`: Child categories. Children have the same JSON structure as the parent and taxonomies can be arbitrarily deeply nested.
